They gather at every place Appetite has been — the Adachi car park, the Ota stairwell, the loading-yard crater, the Shirahige cold store — and, after Chapter 5, in a dorm full of teenagers who lost somebody.

GRADES — Kegare and sorcerers are both graded Four (lowest) to One, and above One there is "unranked," which means "do not."

HOW A SORCERER WORKS — a Sumi pool per long rest; an inherited technique (the Mibu shape their own blood; the Kagura make beasts out of hand-shadows; the Shirasagi do something nobody can explain); VEILS; REVERSE INK, which heals, for the rare few who can; PACTS — declare a restriction aloud and gain power while you keep it; and, for the very strongest, an ENCLOSURE: a space of their own in which their technique cannot miss. Kuroshiki always hunt in pairs: "one to see, one to cut."

KEGARE AND QUIRKS — quirk attacks hurt Kegare at half damage. Radiant damage and Sumi hurt them fully. Somebody who has seen a Kegare once can always see them afterwards.

PEOPLE — MIBU TSUBAKI (sixteen, blood technique, prickly, brilliant) and KAGURA ICHIRŌ (seventeen, shadow hounds, sleepy, "the one who sees") — a pair since they were nine. SHIRASAGI REI — twenty-eight, the Shirasagi heir, sunglasses indoors, so strong it is a joke and so annoying about it that it is a worse one; he teaches at Kurama, he is not a fight, and he thinks Ando's sunglasses show good character.

WHAT A PC CAN EARN — INK-LENS GLASSES (see Kegare and Veils without Sumi); A PACT, taught by Tsubaki: once per long rest, declare a restriction aloud at the start of a fight; while you keep it, +1 to your quirk save DC and +1d8 damage once per turn; break it and take 2d8 psychic and lose the bonus. An invitation to Kurama, which Sugitsu will refuse to sign.

AN OPTIONAL SEED, FOR THE DM ONLY — Kinji Hamakida's registered quirk, Jackpot Fever, behaves an awful lot like a technique: a ritual gesture, a gamble with fixed odds, a song. When Shirasagi Rei reads it on the festival archive, he says "huh." You never have to explain why. If you want to, the Hamakida were a Kuroshiki family that left the rite in 1931 and, within two generations, forgot they had ever been one — but the technique did not forget them. Use this only if it delights you, and never on the spine.

appendix.heading: The Ledger
appendix.body:
THE LEDGER — the fourth door, after Bleach: a civil service of death-gods with swords that have names, a filing system older than the registry, and a backlog.

WHO THEY ARE — a department. That is their own word for it. The Ledger has collected the dead of this city since the Heian court first wrote a date next to a name, and it does the work the way any department does: in rounds, on a schedule, with forms, in black uniforms, politely. Its wardens carry a WRIT — a blade that has a name and will not be used by anybody it has not agreed with — and they are not alive while on duty, which is why nobody has ever looked at one twice.

WHY NOBODY KNOWS — because everybody has seen them. They wear black, they are courteous, and they turn up at accidents. Cameras record a warden as a smudge, the way a dust mote reads. Anybody who can see one clearly is assumed to have a perception quirk and is written down as having one, and the Ledger files that too. There is no conspiracy. There is a department that has never once needed to hide, because hero society documents everything it can see and has stopped wondering about the rest.

WHAT HAS CHANGED — nothing, which is the problem. The Ledger is in arrears. Tokyo has thirty-seven million people in its commuter belt and the Ledger's establishment was set at four hundred wardens in 1869 and has never been revised, because a revision needs a countersignature from a Desk that has been vacant since the war. So things go uncollected, and a thing left uncollected goes wrong.

RANKS — RUNNER (a satchel, a bicycle, notices; no writ yet) · CLERK (a writ, a round, a district) · HAND (a seal, and the authority to collect an Arrear by force) · DESK (one of the Thirteen, and each Desk is a jurisdiction) · the FIRST DESK (who holds the book everybody is in).

ARREARS — a soul that was not collected on time, and has been waiting, and has got bad at being a person. Graded by how overdue: a MONTH, a YEAR, a CENTURY. They do not hunt; they wait, in the place they were told to wait, which is why Tokyo is full of things standing very still in stairwells and under barriers. Quirk damage is halved against an Arrear. Radiant, Sumi and a writ hurt it fully.

HOW A WARDEN WORKS — a WRIT, which is a sword with a name, and which has a FIRST READING (the name, spoken; the blade's one trick) and, for a Desk, a SECOND READING (the office; the blade becomes what the warden's jurisdiction actually is, and the street stops being a street). A SEAL, which is permission; no warden may act outside their writ's jurisdiction without a countersignature, and a warden who does is in arrears themselves. And a LEDGER PAGE for every person in their round, which is a name, a date, and a column.

THE PAPERWORK IS THE WEAKNESS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE FACTION. A Hand standing six feet from something that is nine months overdue, with a writ he cannot draw because the countersignature is in a vacant Desk's in-tray, is the Ledger in one image. They are not frightening because they are cruel. They are frightening because they are punctual, and because they have already closed your file.

PEOPLE — HIBINO ASA, Runner of the Ninth Round: fifteen, has been fifteen since 1998, does a notice round on a bicycle, cheerful, chatty, immaculate records, and the first of them anybody ever speaks to. KAJIURA, Hand of the Fourth Desk: enormous, silent, carries a writ called Second Frost, and will not draw it without permission. SHIROUZU GENBEI: struck off in 1954, runs a sweet shop in Yanaka, was a Desk once, sells things a living person should not be able to buy, and will forge a countersignature for a price that is not money. TŌNO SHIGEMORI, the FIRST DESK: holds the book. Will answer exactly one question truthfully. The price is a page with your name on it.

WHAT A PC CAN EARN — A MARK, inked on the back of the hand by a Runner: you can see wardens, writs and Arrears, permanently, and cameras still cannot. A COUNTERSIGNATURE, once per long rest: name a creature aloud; for one minute your attacks against it ignore Overdue and Born of Dread, and once per turn you add 1d8 force. The price of both is a page, and a page is not a debt and not a curse — it is a date, left blank, in a book that is never wrong.

WHO IT FIGHTS — THE KUROSHIKI, over jurisdiction, bitterly and constantly. A Kegare is dread; an Arrear is a person; and there are things in this city that are both, and neither side will sign for the other's, so those things stand where they are. THE SCARLET LEGION, hopelessly: every vampire in Ginza is centuries in arrears and the Ledger has never collected one, and the First Desk's book has exactly one page with no date on it at all, and it is Lady Akabane Seraphine's. THE ASTRAL COURT, politely and on good terms: Sunbreath is breath, and breath is something the Ledger counts, and the two departments have an understanding that is older than Japan's current constitution.

THE HARD LIMIT, AS FOR EVERY FACTION — the Ledger is not behind Appetite, did not know what Appetite was, and could not have stopped it. It collected four of the five, on time, correctly, and closed the file, because there is no field on the form for how somebody died. Never soften that and never apologise for it. It is the fourth faction's entire reason to exist in this campaign.

AN OPTIONAL SEED, FOR THE DM ONLY — a writ agrees with its bearer, which is a thing no quirk has ever done. If you want the fourth door to touch the first three, the answer is Hiro: a frame with nobody in it, walking around a city where the Ledger's whole job is knowing who is where. Asa has seen him twice and has written both times in the margin, with a question mark, because he does not have a page. Use this only if it delights you, and never on the spine.

appendix.heading: Stat blocks — the Underground
appendix.body:
Numbers for the three factions. Two entries — the Legate and Shirasagi Rei — are written as warnings rather than fights, and should stay that way. All of them are in the encounter manager under "Underground."

LEGION THRALL — CR 1/2
Somebody the Scarlet Legion fed from and did not finish. Grey, slow, silent, always in numbers. Hellsing's ghouls, in a Tokyo dock.
AC 11 · HP 22 · Speed 25 ft · Initiative +0
STR 14 · DEX 10 · CON 14 · INT 3 · WIS 6 · CHA 3
· CLAW (+4) — 1d8+2 slashing. On a hit, CON DC 11 or gain a rank of Queasy.
· MINDLESS — immune to being charmed or frightened; obeys the nearest Legion vampire.
· SUNLIGHT — crumbles to ash at the end of any turn it spends in direct sunlight.
· ONCE A PERSON — they were somebody. A private clinic in Minato has the records of who.
· HOW TO RUN — Six at a time, out of the dark, at the wharf. The horror is that they are slow and do not stop.

LEGIONARY (SCARLET LEGION) — CR 4
A turned vampire of the Legion's rank and file. Often recruited from people who were already strong — some of them used to be Byakko.
AC 14 · HP 60 · Speed 35 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 13
STR 16 · DEX 16 · CON 16 · INT 12 · WIS 12 · CHA 15
· CLAW (+6) — 2d8+3 slashing.
· BITE (+6) — 2d6+3 piercing + 2d6 necrotic. It regains HP equal to the necrotic damage dealt.
· REGENERATION — regains 10 HP at the start of its turn unless it took radiant, fire or silver damage since its last turn.
· GAZE (action) — one creature within 30 ft, WIS DC 13 or charmed for 1 minute (treats the Legionary as a trusted friend).
· MIST (once per night) — becomes mist until its next turn: fly 30 ft, passes through gaps, immune to non-radiant damage.
· WEAKNESSES — in direct sunlight: no regeneration, 4d6 radiant at the start of each turn, disadvantage on everything. Vulnerable to radiant and silver. Cannot enter a private home uninvited. Cannot cross running water unaided.
· HOW TO RUN — Claw then bite, every turn, on the same target. Ren Suzuki's beam is radiant — the Legion will know what that means before he does.

MINA TODA, CENTURION OF THE SCARLET LEGION — CR 7
Looks nineteen. Has looked nineteen since 1923. The Legion's diplomat and recruiter, and almost certainly the first of them a PC ever speaks to — at a party, holding a glass of something red she does not drink.
AC 16 · HP 105 · Speed 40 ft · Initiative +4 · Save DC 15
STR 16 · DEX 18 · CON 16 · INT 16 · WIS 15 · CHA 20
· MULTIATTACK — TWO CLAW STRIKES (+8) — 2d10+4 slashing each.
· BITE (+8) — 2d8+4 piercing + 3d6 necrotic. She regains HP equal to the necrotic damage.
· REGENERATION 15 — as a Legionary.
· GAZE — WIS DC 15.
· RESTRICTION RELEASE (bonus action) — she fights sealed at Level Three. Each release (Three → Two → One) gives +2 to hit and damage and 20 temporary HP, and makes her stranger to look at: by Level One her shadow has eyes in it.
· WEAKNESSES — as a Legionary.
· HOW TO RUN — Talks first, always. Would much rather recruit a PC than fight one, and is honest about what the offer costs, which is the frightening part.

CAPTAIN GRAU, CENTURION OF THE SCARLET LEGION — CR 9
The Legion's soldier. Seven feet, grey greatcoat, has not spoken since 1945. The Legion sends Grau when talking has failed.
AC 17 · HP 170 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +1 · Save DC 16
STR 22 · DEX 12 · CON 20 · INT 10 · WIS 13 · CHA 8
· MULTIATTACK — TWO FISTS (+9) — 3d10+6 bludgeoning each.
· REGENERATION 15 — as a Legionary.
· UNBROKEN — the first time each night he would drop to 0 HP, he drops to 1 instead.
· RESTRICTION RELEASE — as Mina Toda.
· WEAKNESSES — as a Legionary.
· HOW TO RUN — Walks forward. Hits whatever is in front of him. Stops when told to.

LADY AKABANE SERAPHINE, LEGATE OF THE SCARLET LEGION — CR 14
Four hundred years old, looks thirty, runs the Legion from the Crimson Room in Ginza. Unfailingly courteous. Has outlived eleven generations of heroes and considers hero society a phase.
AC 19 · HP 260 · Speed 40 ft, fly 40 ft · Initiative +5 · Save DC 19
STR 20 · DEX 20 · CON 22 · INT 20 · WIS 18 · CHA 24
· MULTIATTACK — THREE CLAWS (+12) — 3d10+7 slashing each.
· BITE (+12) — 3d8+7 piercing + 4d8 necrotic.
· REGENERATION 25.
· GAZE — every creature of her choice within 30 ft, WIS DC 19.
· LEVEL ZERO (once) — she stops being a person-shaped thing, and four shadow hounds step out of her coat (AC 15, 30 HP, bite +10 for 2d10+5).
· NOT A FIGHT — she is beyond the party at any level this campaign reaches. She is a negotiation, and the campaign treats her as one.
· HOW TO RUN — She does not fight students. She invites them to dinner, and the danger is in what she offers.

DAYBREAK INITIATE (ASTRAL COURT) — CR 1
A first-rung student of Sunbreath. Registered Quirkless, and proud of it. Trained in a bathhouse.
AC 13 · HP 22 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +2 · Save DC 12
STR 12 · DEX 14 · CON 14 · INT 11 · WIS 13 · CHA 10
· SUNBREATH STRIKE (+4) — 1d6+2 bludgeoning + 1d6 radiant.
· SUNBREATH (3 per short rest) — add 1d6 radiant to a hit; or walk on water or up a wall until the end of the turn; or heal 1d8 by touch. Against a Legion vampire the heal deals 2d8 radiant instead.
· BREATH IS EVERYTHING — gagged, choked or underwater without a breath, Sunbreath stops working.
· HOW TO RUN — Defensive, polite, and absolutely certain the PCs are about to be eaten by something.

HŌSHŌ KAITO & PAPER PLANES (ENVOY-BEARER) — CR 5
Seventeen, night clerk at a Kōenji convenience store, magnificent pompadour, extremely polite until you mention his hair.
AC 15 · HP 75 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 14
STR 13 · DEX 16 · CON 14 · INT 12 · WIS 13 · CHA 16
· MULTIATTACK — PAPER PLANES' FISTS (+7, 10 ft) — 2d8+3 bludgeoning each.
· ENVOY: PAPER PLANES — Power B · Speed B · Range D · Durability C · Precision B · Potential A. Anything it punches folds like paper for one minute: a door becomes a crane, a car folds flat, a wall folds open. A creature it hits makes a CON DC 14 save or is folded flat (incapacitated, speed 0) until the end of its next turn.
· ENVOY RULES — an Envoy can only be hurt by another Envoy or by radiant damage, and damage dealt to it is dealt to its bearer. Hit Kaito.
· SUNBREATH (4 per short rest).
· HOW TO RUN — A good kid who has been fighting a war nobody told him was optional. The likeliest Court friend for the class.

GRANDMOTHER HINATA SAE, ELDER OF THE ASTRAL COURT — CR 10
Eighty-one, runs the Matsu-no-Yu bathhouse in Kōenji. The rumour is that she can stay underwater for ten minutes. The rumour is wrong. It is twelve.
AC 17 · HP 140 · Speed 35 ft · Initiative +4 · Save DC 17
STR 12 · DEX 18 · CON 16 · INT 15 · WIS 20 · CHA 16
· MULTIATTACK — TWO SUNBREATH PALMS (+10) — 2d8+4 bludgeoning + 3d8 radiant each.
· SUNBREATH (unlimited).
· OVERDRIVE (recharge 5–6) — a 30-ft line of sunlight carried through water or metal: DEX DC 17, 8d8 radiant. Legion vampires save at disadvantage and take double.
· NO ENVOY — she never wanted one. She has buried three students who did.
· HOW TO RUN — She will test a PC, not fight one: a slap that hurts like sunburn, and then a question about how they breathe.

SAOTOME SHIN & BAD MOON, THE ARROWHEAD THIEF — CR 8
Thirty-four, a former Courtier who believes Envoys should belong to the strong. Byakko's ladder of power is his idea of heaven, and he has been feeding it.
AC 16 · HP 120 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 16
STR 14 · DEX 16 · CON 16 · INT 15 · WIS 12 · CHA 15
· MULTIATTACK — BAD MOON'S FISTS (+8, 10 ft) — 3d8+3 bludgeoning each.
· THE ARROWHEAD (+8) — 1d4 piercing. CON DC 16. Success: the target awakens an Envoy within the week. Failure: it drops to 0 HP and begins dying.
· ENVOY: BAD MOON — Power B · Speed C · Range C · Durability A · Precision C · Potential E. ECLIPSE: within 30 ft of Bad Moon, light sources go out and radiant damage and Sunbreath stop working.
· ENVOY RULES — as Hōshō Kaito.
· He has been cutting Byakko fighters with a stolen arrowhead since spring. Saeki Momo is one of the ones who lived.
· HOW TO RUN — The Court storyline's villain if you want one. Fights from inside his Eclipse so that nothing the Court taught can touch him.

KEGARE, GRADE FOUR — CR 1/2
A knot of somebody's fear that has learned to move. A thing in a stairwell. Mostly harmless. Mostly.
AC 12 · HP 18 · Speed 30 ft, climb 30 ft · Initiative +2
STR 10 · DEX 14 · CON 12 · INT 2 · WIS 10 · CHA 3
· GRASP (+4) — 2d4 necrotic.
· UNSEEN — invisible to anybody without Sumi, and it does not appear on cameras.
· BORN OF DREAD — resistance to all damage except radiant and Sumi-infused attacks.
· HOW TO RUN — They gather where people have been afraid: hospitals, crime scenes, every place Appetite has ever been.

KEGARE, GRADE TWO — CR 5
Big enough to be a problem and old enough to talk. It speaks in the voice of whatever fear made it.
AC 14 · HP 85 · Speed 40 ft · Initiative +2 · Save DC 14
STR 18 · DEX 14 · CON 16 · INT 6 · WIS 12 · CHA 6
· MULTIATTACK — TWO LIMBS (+7) — 2d10+4 bludgeoning each.
· UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD — as Grade Four.
· DREAD (recharge 5–6) — every creature within 30 ft that can perceive it makes a WIS DC 14 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.
· FEAR FEEDS IT — whenever a creature within 30 ft fails a save against being frightened, it regains 10 HP.
· HOW TO RUN — Picks the most frightened person in the room and stays on them.

KEGARE, GRADE ONE — "THE ROLL CALL" — CR 9
Born in the Heights Alliance ground-floor corridor out of a class that lost somebody. It counts.
AC 16 · HP 170 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 17
STR 18 · DEX 16 · CON 20 · INT 8 · WIS 16 · CHA 10
· MULTIATTACK — TWO GRASPS (+9) — 3d10+4 necrotic each.
· UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD — as Grade Four.
· COUNTING — at the start of each round it counts the people in the room aloud, in the voice of whoever started the roll call in the loading yard, and loses its place, and starts again. Every creature that hears it makes a WIS DC 17 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.
· FED — it regains 15 HP whenever a creature within 60 ft fails a save against being frightened.
· HOW TO RUN — Run it only if the table has the appetite — see the safety note in "The Thing in the Laundry Room." It is beaten by people who refuse to be counted: anybody who answers the count out loud with their own name is immune to Counting for the rest of the fight.

MIBU TSUBAKI, KUROSHIKI SORCERER (GRADE TWO) — CR 5
Sixteen, prickly, the Mibu house's best student in a generation and painfully aware of it. Hunts in a pair, like every Kuroshiki: "one to see, one to cut."
AC 15 · HP 70 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 15
STR 12 · DEX 16 · CON 14 · INT 14 · WIS 14 · CHA 12
· BLOOD LANCE — TWO LANCES (+7, 60 ft) — 3d8 piercing each.
· SUMI (8 per long rest).
· MIBU BLOOD RITE — Red Bind (bonus action, 1 Sumi): STR DC 15 or restrained. Clot (reaction, 2 Sumi): halve the damage of one hit.
· VEIL (action, 2 Sumi) — a black dome up to 100 ft across. From outside, nothing is happening, and cameras record an empty street.
· PACT (once per fight) — she declares a restriction aloud ("I will not move from this spot") and gains +2 to her save DC and +1d10 on Blood Lance while she keeps it.
· HOW TO RUN — Will tell U.A. students to go home, twice, and then need their help.

KAGURA ICHIRŌ, KUROSHIKI SORCERER (GRADE TWO) — CR 5
Seventeen, sleepy, polite, and Tsubaki's partner since they were nine. He does the seeing; she does the cutting.
AC 14 · HP 72 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +2 · Save DC 15
STR 12 · DEX 14 · CON 14 · INT 13 · WIS 17 · CHA 12
· SHADOW-HOUND BITE (EACH HOUND) (+6) — 2d8+3 piercing.
· SUMI (8 per long rest).
· KAGURA SHADOW RITE — Hound (bonus action, 2 Sumi): a shadow hound forms from his hand-shadow (AC 13, 25 HP), lasting 1 minute; at most two.
· THE ONE WHO SEES — he can see Kegare from a mile away and always knows where the nearest one is.
· HOW TO RUN — Stays behind Tsubaki and points. Gets on quietly well with Kibi Kankei, for reasons neither of them examines.

SHIRASAGI REI, UNRANKED KUROSHIKI SORCERER — CR 15
Twenty-eight, heir of the Shirasagi house, wears sunglasses indoors, extraordinarily strong and extraordinarily annoying about it. Teaches at the Kurama Rite School. Thinks Ando Iorai's sunglasses show good character.
AC 20 · HP 250 · Speed 40 ft · Initiative +6 · Save DC 20
STR 16 · DEX 22 · CON 18 · INT 20 · WIS 18 · CHA 20
· ANYTHING HE LIKES (+13) — 4d10+6 force.
· THE LONG WAY ROUND — he can make the distance between himself and anything he chooses impossible to cross. Attacks against him do not arrive unless he allows them to.
· ENCLOSURE: THE LONG CORRIDOR (once per day) — a 60-ft sphere; every creature inside is walking down an endless corridor toward him and is incapacitated for 1 minute (WIS DC 20 at the end of each turn).
· NOT A FIGHT — like the Legate, he is beyond this campaign. He is a mentor, a warning, and a very irritating lunch.
· HOW TO RUN — Never fights the class. Shows up, makes an enormous problem disappear in one move, eats somebody's snack, and leaves.

appendix.heading: Stat blocks — the Ledger
appendix.body:
Numbers for the fourth faction. Two entries — the First Desk and Shirouzu Genbei — are written as negotiations rather than fights and should stay that way. All of them are in the encounter manager under "Underground."

THE ONE RULE THAT APPLIES TO ALL OF THEM — FILED: a warden on duty does not appear on any camera or recording, and anybody without a Mark, a Sumi pool, or recent proximity to their own death sees only a person in black they will not remember. Quirk attacks still hit them perfectly well. They are not ghosts. They are staff.

ARREAR, ONE MONTH OVERDUE — CR 1
Somebody who was not collected on time and has been standing where they were told to stand for five weeks. Still mostly shaped like a person, which is worse.
AC 12 · HP 30 · Speed 20 ft · Initiative +0
STR 14 · DEX 10 · CON 14 · INT 6 · WIS 8 · CHA 5
· GRASP (+4) — 2d6+2 necrotic.
· OVERDUE — quirk damage is halved against it. Radiant damage, Sumi-infused attacks and writs hurt it fully.
· WAITING — it cannot willingly move more than 30 ft from the spot it was told to wait in, and it will not pursue. It also will not stop.
· HOW TO RUN — It does not hunt. It stands in a stairwell, or under a barrier, or at the back of a hospital car park, and anybody who comes within reach is within reach.

ARREAR, ONE YEAR OVERDUE — CR 4
Twelve months of standing still. It has stopped having a face and started having a direction.
AC 14 · HP 70 · Speed 25 ft · Initiative +1 · Save DC 13
STR 17 · DEX 12 · CON 16 · INT 5 · WIS 9 · CHA 5
· MULTIATTACK — TWO GRASPS (+6) — 2d8+3 necrotic each.
· OVERDUE and WAITING — as above.
· STILL DUE (recharge 5–6) — it says the date it was supposed to be collected on. Every creature within 20 ft makes a WIS DC 13 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.
· HOW TO RUN — Immobile, relentless, and loud about one number. The fight is a positioning puzzle, not a chase.

ARREAR, NINE MONTHS OVERDUE — "THE ONE UNDER THE BARRIER" — CR 8
The Yanaka level crossing. Nine months in the four inches of space under the barrier arm, because that is where it was told to wait, and nobody came, because the Rite calls it a Kegare and the Ledger calls it an Arrear and nobody will sign.
AC 15 · HP 120 · Speed 25 ft · Initiative +2 · Save DC 15
STR 18 · DEX 14 · CON 18 · INT 6 · WIS 11 · CHA 6
· MULTIATTACK — THREE GRASPS (+8, 15 ft reach) — 2d10+4 necrotic each.
· OVERDUE and WAITING — as above, and it will not leave the crossing under any circumstances, including to save itself.
· BOTH AND NEITHER — it is an Arrear and a Kegare at once. It is Unseen without Sumi or a Mark, it is Born of Dread, and it is Overdue, and the three rules stack, which is exactly why nobody has dealt with it.
· FOUR MINUTES (at the start of each round) — the barriers come down. Everything within 20 ft of the rails is pushed 10 ft toward the crossing (STR DC 15 to resist), and then a train goes over, and then they go up.
· HOW TO RUN — Contact scene in Chapter 8, "Nobody Signed For It." It is not a hard fight for a party at level 11; it is a strange one. Two wardens will watch and will not help, and will be helpful about it.

ARREAR, A CENTURY OVERDUE — CR 13
A hundred and ten years at the back of a building that was knocked down in 1962. There is no person left in it and there is still a date.
AC 17 · HP 210 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +3 · Save DC 18
STR 21 · DEX 16 · CON 20 · INT 8 · WIS 14 · CHA 8
· MULTIATTACK — FOUR GRASPS (+10) — 3d10+5 necrotic each.
· OVERDUE — as above. BORN OF DREAD, if you want it both ways.
· WAITING, STILL — a 60-ft radius it has not left since the Occupation. Inside it, the Arrear has advantage on everything. Outside it, it cannot go.
· THE WRONG DATE (recharge 5–6) — it says a date. Every creature within 40 ft makes a WIS DC 18 save or takes 6d8 psychic and is frightened for 1 minute; on a save, half and no fear. A creature that answers with its own name is immune to The Wrong Date for the rest of the fight.
· HOW TO RUN — Only if a third season wants it. It is the Ledger's version of the Roll Call: beaten by people who refuse to be a number, and by nothing else.

HIBINO ASA, RUNNER OF THE NINTH ROUND — CR 2
Fifteen, and has been fifteen since 1998. A satchel, a bicycle, a pencil she licks, and the best records in the department. She has no writ, because Runners do not get one, and she has asked four times.
AC 14 · HP 40 · Speed 35 ft · Initiative +4 · Save DC 12
STR 10 · DEX 18 · CON 12 · INT 14 · WIS 15 · CHA 16
· NOTICE (+6) — 1d6+4 force. She hits people with a rolled-up form. It works better than it should.
· FILED — as above.
· THE ROUND — she knows where every Arrear in her district is standing, and how long it has been there, and will tell anybody who asks politely.
· A MARK (action, once per day) — she inks a character on the back of a willing creature's hand. They can see wardens, writs and Arrears permanently. It costs them a page. She will explain that clearly first, every time, because she is not allowed to and does it anyway.
· HOW TO RUN — Not a fight. The friendliest thing in the Underground and the single most upsetting, because she has four of the Case 9 names in her notebook with ticks against them and she filed them correctly and wants to know whether there was a problem with it.

KAJIURA, HAND OF THE FOURTH DESK — CR 9
Seven feet, black uniform, a writ called SECOND FROST, and a Desk above him that has been vacant since 1945, which means his countersignatures come from nowhere and most of his authority is theoretical.
AC 17 · HP 150 · Speed 30 ft · Initiative +2 · Save DC 16
STR 20 · DEX 14 · CON 18 · INT 12 · WIS 16 · CHA 10
· WRIT: SECOND FROST (+9) — 3d10+5 slashing + 2d10 cold. Hurts an Arrear or a Kegare fully.
· FIRST READING — "Second Frost, settle." Once per fight, a 30-ft cone: DEX DC 16 or 4d10 cold and speed 0 until the end of its next turn.
· FILED — as above.
· NO COUNTERSIGNATURE — he will not draw Second Frost outside his jurisdiction, and almost nothing in Tokyo is inside it. He is a CR 9 stat block standing perfectly still with his hands at his sides, and that is not a bug.
· WITH A COUNTERSIGNATURE — forged, granted, or signed by a PC who did not read the form — he is the best ally in the Underground and ends most fights in two rounds.
· HOW TO RUN — One sentence per scene, maximum, and always a procedural observation. The sentence he says when a PC is about to die is the most useful thing anybody says all chapter.

SHIROUZU GENBEI, STRUCK OFF — CR 11
Struck off the Ledger in 1954 for a countersignature he wrote himself. Runs a sweet shop in Yanaka, three streets from the crossing, and sells rice crackers to schoolchildren and other things to other people. Was a Desk. Still writes like one.
AC 18 · HP 180 · Speed 35 ft · Initiative +5 · Save DC 17
STR 14 · DEX 20 · CON 16 · INT 18 · WIS 18 · CHA 17
· WRIT: LONG SUMMER (+10) — 4d8+5 slashing. It still answers to him, which is technically theft.
· STRUCK OFF — he is not Filed. Cameras see him. He pays tax. He finds this hilarious.
· A COUNTERSIGNATURE, FORGED (ritual, one hour) — indistinguishable from a real one. His price is never money: a favour, an errand, a true answer to a question he asks, or a jar of something from the Astral Court's bathhouse.
· NOT A FIGHT — he is the Ledger's way in and its only sympathetic authority. Treat him as Urahara: a shopkeeper who used to run a department and will not say which one.
· HOW TO RUN — Delighted to see visitors. Sells them something cheap first. Tells them the truth in the wrong order.

TŌNO SHIGEMORI, THE FIRST DESK — CR 16
Holds the book. Everybody in the city is in it, on a page, with a date, and the dates are not wrong. Unfailingly polite, entirely without malice, and the least negotiable thing in this campaign.
AC 20 · HP 280 · Speed 40 ft · Initiative +6 · Save DC 20
STR 18 · DEX 22 · CON 20 · INT 22 · WIS 22 · CHA 20
· WRIT: THE WHOLE OF IT (+13) — 4d12+6 force.
· SECOND READING: THE DEPARTMENT (once) — a 120-ft radius becomes his jurisdiction. Inside it, he cannot be surprised, cannot be moved, and no creature may take the Dash action; and every creature inside hears its own page read out.
· ONE QUESTION — he will answer exactly one question truthfully, to anybody who reaches him. The price is a page with their name on it, and he will tell them so, and he will not tell them the date.
· NOT A FIGHT — like the Legate and Shirasagi Rei, he is beyond any level this module reaches, and he is a negotiation. The campaign treats him as one.
· HOW TO RUN — He does not threaten and he does not bargain. He has an appointment at eleven. The horror is entirely in how reasonable he is about the price.

appendix.heading: Room for more — building the next faction
appendix.body:
The Underground is built to grow. Here is how to add a faction in an evening, the way the first three were built — each from an anime its DM loved.

THE TEMPLATE
· AN INSPIRATION — one series you love. The Legion is Hellsing, the Court is JoJo, the Kuroshiki are Jujutsu Kaisen. Take its feeling, not its names.
· WHY NOBODY NOTICED — the answer is always the registry: in a world where everybody has a quirk, what does this power get mistaken for?
· ONE RESOURCE, ONE SIGNATURE, ONE WEAKNESS — Blood and regeneration and sunlight. Sunbreath and an Envoy and breath. Sumi and a technique and the fact that they cannot be seen. Three rules is enough.
· RANKS — five, from bottom to top, with names that sound like the faction.
· A HAUNT — one place in Tokyo where its Odd Night band widens to 01–10.
· THE LADDER — a rumour, a trace, a witness scene, a contact scene and an invitation.
· THREE PEOPLE — somebody friendly, somebody frightening, and somebody who is a negotiation rather than a fight.
· WHAT A PC CAN EARN — one feature, balanced like Sunbreath or a Pact: small, flavourful, a little better on the right character.
· WHO IT FIGHTS — every faction should have an enemy among the others. It is where seasons come from.
· THE RULE — never on the spine.

THREE UNCLAIMED RUMOURS, IF YOU WANT A STARTING POINT
· "A fishmonger at Tsukiji hasn't aged a day since 1964, and neither has anybody who works his stall."
· "There's a road on the Shuto Expressway that isn't on any map. Motorbikes with no lights ride it at four in the morning, and the riders wear masks."
· "There's a teahouse in Yanaka where you can buy a dream. The price is one of yours."

Give any of them a name and an anime, and you have a fourth door.

FOUR DOORS ARE PAINTED NOW. The Scarlet Legion (Hellsing), the Astral Court (JoJo), the Kuroshiki (Jujutsu Kaisen) and the Ledger (Bleach) are all written up, with ladders, stat blocks and a contact scene each. The template above built all four and it will build a fifth.

AND THE FIFTH SPACE IS STILL EMPTY, which is deliberate. Two of the three unclaimed rumours above are still unclaimed:
· "A fishmonger at Tsukiji hasn't aged a day since 1964, and neither has anybody who works his stall."
· "There's a teahouse in Yanaka where you can buy a dream. The price is one of yours."

The third — the unlit motorbikes on a road that is not on any map — is yours to use or to leave; nothing in the module has taken it.

ONE NOTE FROM BUILDING THE FOURTH — the Ledger worked because its "why nobody noticed" was not concealment at all. Everybody has seen them. They wear black and turn up at accidents. The best answer to the registry question is usually the most boring one available, and the most frightening faction in this module is the one that files on time.

AND GIVE YOUR FIFTH FACTION AN ENEMY AMONG THE OTHER FOUR. The Legion and the Court have been at war since 1868. The Kuroshiki and the Ledger will not sign for each other's work and there are things standing in the gaps all over Tokyo because of it. The Court and the Ledger are politely on excellent terms, which annoys everybody. That is where seasons come from.

appendix.heading: The shop — new stock, and what it is for
appendix.body:
The shop page has new stock for this edition — non-lethal and capture gear for provisional students who are not allowed to hurt anybody, traditional weapons, gadgets, consumables, and a leisure section for free time. A few things in it are more useful than they look, and you should be delighted, not annoyed, when a player finds them.

THE ONES TO WATCH FOR
· EARPLUGS (¥200) — Riddle can only work on somebody who can hear him. A player who buys these has read him better than the Commission did. Let it work, every time, and remind them they are now deaf.
· COOLING SPRAY and INSTANT ICE PACKS — end Izuto's stall. They cost an ally's action, which is the pair rule in miniature.
· HYDRATION PACK — Masahata's Water Gun depends on it, and so does anybody whose quirk drinks.
· SMELLING SALTS — clear a rank of Concussed. Rawagi Chiso will need a great many in Chapter 5.
· COMMS EARPIECES — excellent everywhere except the Shirahige cold store, where the refrigerant lining eats the signal between floors. Tell them the first time they try.
· RUBBER ROUNDS, CAPTURE TAPE, STUN BATON, RIOT SHIELD — legal-ish tools for a class that is not allowed to hurt anybody in a backstreet. Byakko will find them hilarious and then very annoying.

HOW THE PRICES WERE BALANCED — against the handbook's own curve: damage tracks price (a 1d4 knife is ¥6,000, a 2d6 katana ¥85,000), non-lethal and control options cost more per die than lethal ones because they are better for students, single-use consumables are cheap, and anything that changes a fight's action economy is priced like a weapon.

WHAT IS NOT IN THE SHOP — anything from the Underground. Sunbreath, Pacts, ink-lens glasses, silvered weapons and Alucard's card are rewards you hand out, never things anybody can buy. Keeping them off the shop page is what keeps the Underground hidden.
